In design — your say first

BLKOUT is designing something — and asking you first

Ivor's Table

Dinner, the way Ivor Cummings used to do it — revived for Black queer men across the generations. Nothing is fixed yet. That's where you come in.

The idea

The table does the work.

Ivor Cummings met the Windrush at Tilbury — and fed a generation of Black men finding their feet in Britain at his famous Friday-night table. We want to set it again: a shared meal that carries a conversation most of us have never had — about prostate health, our bodies, our fathers, and looking after each other. No clinic. No lecture. No leaflet first.

Black queer men carry more than double the population risk of prostate cancer — and nobody's campaign is built for the rooms we trust. So we're designing the room. With you.

The evening — as sketched

Eighteen of us. Three tables of six.

  • The roomA private dining room in south London — ours for the night, minutes from a well-connected station.
  • The mealFamily-style, from Black diaspora kitchens — Caribbean, West African, Brazilian, South African, African American — cooked by a Black chef.
  • The shufflePlace cards re-deal between courses. By dessert you've broken bread with most of the room.
  • The turnA trained voice joins as a guest — and everyone does the 30-second risk checker together, phones out. Normalised, collective, done.
  • The send-offYou leave with dessert boxed for one more man in your life, its recipe, and a promise to share a meal with him. Each one teach one.

We think a seat lands around £37, everyone paying their own way — and if price is ever the problem, it quietly isn't. You'd tell us, and it's handled.

Before anything is fixed — three questions

Help us design it.

  • 01 — What appeals, if anything?
  • 02 — What would actually get you to come?
  • 03 — What would put you off, or what have we missed?

Reply with as much or as little as you like. And if you already know you'd want a seat at the first table — say that too.
